## Sonic Engineering: Touhou on Vintage Hardware

The intersection of nostalgia and technical ingenuity remains a strong theme in this week’s digest, particularly within the *Touhou Project* community. We are seeing a fascinating divide between high-energy fan arrangements and low-level hardware optimization.

On the creative side, the *Touhou Music* group 〘東方Wave〙 has released a new arranged track titled "Beast Metropolis," specifically the vocal version featuring xi-on. Titled "Aya ~xi-on~," this single drops a direct link to the YouTube host, offering fans a fresh take on the series' iconic soundtracks. It is a straightforward release, serving as a pure distribution point for the music without accompanying debate or extensive commentary, allowing the arrangement to stand on its own merits.

However, the technical highlight comes from user @Seledreams, who has documented a convoluted but effective workflow for bringing PC-98 *Touhou* music patches to the legendary Yamaha DX7 synthesizer. The process involves extracting VGZ rips from VGMrips, converting them to Sega Genesis YM2612 .TFI files using `opna2tfi`, and packing them into an OPM file via TFI2OPM. The final step utilizes DXConvert to transform the data into a compatible DX7 patch. Despite the multi-step rigmarole, the author notes that the resulting synthesis is highly effective on the hardware, leveraging the technical similarities between the Sega Genesis and PC-98 audio chips to breathe new life on vintage FM synthesis gear.

## Retro Computing: Stargate Revival for VIC-20

For homebrew enthusiasts, the Commodore VIC-20 has gained a new contender in the arcade adaptation space. @BrewOtaku Magazine shared news of *Stargate*, a complete rebuild of the classic Williams arcade game developed by MilaSoft.

Unlike many ports that rely on emulation layers, this version is written in 100% machine language to maximize performance on the modest hardware. Early impressions highlight smooth scrolling and intelligent enemy behaviors that faithfully recreate the frantic pace of the original. The game supports both one and two-player modes and features a unique hyperspace mechanic. This release adds to the growing library of VIC-20 titles available on itch.io, proving that there is still significant creative energy dedicated to pushing the limits of 8-bit homebrew.

## Photography: DIY Bellows and Wet Plate Warmth

The photography community on 4chan’s /gg/ (Gear General) board is buzzing with DIY projects and analog revivalism. The most ambitious undertaking is a user 3D printing a bellows camera designed to utilize obsolete "postcard" format lenses. By creating a custom device for 6x12 to 6x17 film, the creator aims to bridge vintage optics with modern manufacturing, offering a cost-effective alternative for large format photography.

Simultaneously, the "wet plate" subculture continues to thrive. One thread features a "wet plate chud edition" project that has garnered praise for its aesthetic appeal and technical demands. The community is highly engaged, with users prompting the creator for immediate progress shots. This exchange underscores a broader appreciation for the hands-on, tangible results of analog processes in an increasingly digital landscape.

## Community Dynamics: Poll Wars and Banter

Not all discussions are technical. On /gg/, the rivalry between users continues to provide entertainment, centered around poll manipulation. User "Oly anon" is the current target of teasing for his sensitivity and his habit of using multiple VPNs to cast additional "no" votes on unpopular polls. Another user mocks this effort as a "game of pretend" that yields a cheap dopamine hit. This ongoing banter highlights the specific social dynamics and feuds that keep the gear enthusiast community lively, even when the actual gear talk has "gone to shit."

## Quick Hits

*   **Touhou Vocal Release:** 〘東方Wave〙 released "Aya ~xi-on~" on YouTube.
*   **DX7 Conversion:** @Seledreams’ guide for PC-98 to Yamaha DX7 patch conversion is a must-read for synthesizer hobbyists.
*   **Stargate Homebrew:** MilaSoft’s VIC-20 port features smooth scrolling and hyperspace mechanics.
*   **3D Printed Camera:** New DIY bellows camera for 6x17 postcard lenses.
*   **Poll Teasing:** "Oly anon" faces ridicule for VPN vote manipulation on /gg/.
*   **Wet Plate Interest:** High engagement on progress shots for analog collodion projects.

representative_texts: @Seledreams - Touhou Music — Fun fact : You can convert PC-98 Touhou instruments to play on Yamaha DX7 — I recently got a Yamaha DX7 and I thought "the synthesis system is fairly similar to the Sega Genesis and the PC-98, so couldn't it be technically possible to convert PC-98 touhou patches to DX7 patches ?"  And that's actually totally possible !   the way to do it :     Grab the VGZ rips of your choice on vgmrips or another site   Get the VGM files from the VGZ   Convert the VGM to YM2612 .TFI files (the sega genesis format) using opna2tfi   Pack them into an OPM file using TFI2OPM   Convert the OPM to a DX7 patch using DXConvert     it's a little bit convoluted but in the end you end up with the patches converted in a way that works on the DX7 synthesizer just fine.   Posted by u/Seledreams · [comments]

Finally, the OPM file is transformed into a compatible DX7 patch using DXConvert. The author notes that while the method is convoluted, the resulting synthesis works effectively on the hardware due to the technical similarities between the Sega Genesis and PC-98 systems.
